summary: Kamil Zvelebil was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (~1946–1952). He later held posts at the Oriental Institute, ASCR (~1952–1970) and Utrecht University (1980–1990).

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi is an Indology and religious studies scholar who taught Hisayoshi Miyamoto and Shujun Motegi. He held academic posts at Banaras Hindu University and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Kammie Takahashi, a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Mount Holyoke College and the University of Virginia (~2000–2009) under David Germano, Paul Groner, and Daishun Ueyama. She held a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.

Kanai Lal Hazra is a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied under Sukumar Sengupta and earned his PhD at the University of Ceylon (~1964–1968) under Sirima Kiribamune. He served as Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta (~1970).
Kanchu Onoue is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Eizan Gakuin and as a teacher at Hikone Higashi High School.

Kang-nam Oh is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his PhD at McMaster University (~1971–1976) under Yun-hua Jan. He held a post at the University of Regina (~1980–2007).
Kang-yuan Sung is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at the University of Calgary (~1996–1999) under A. W. Barber, and also studied with Anne Moore and Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie, attended the University of Paris (~1928–1934), and held an appointment at Tokyo National Museum.
Kanoko Tanaka is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under traditional teacher Muni Tulsi. She served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University.
Kansei Tamura (1928–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1953) and held a teaching post as a lecturer at Rissho University.

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was an Indology and history scholar educated at the University of Delhi (~1944–1948), University of Michigan (~1948–1949), and Banaras Hindu University. She served as Academic Director at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (~1987–1993).

Karel Werner (1925–2019) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. In 1968, he taught Sanskrit and Indian philosophy and religion at Durham University and Cambridge, and later was an Honorary Professorial Research Associate at SOAS (~1993–2019).

Karen C. Lang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed graduate studies at the University of Washington (ending 1983). She served as a professor at the University of Virginia from around 1982.

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar who taught Johan Elverskog. She completed her studies at Smith College (~1960–1964), Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University (ending ~1976).

Karen Nelson Villanueva is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies in 2013 under James Ryan and Dianne Jenett, and also studied under Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero is a scholar who taught Sally McAra and held academic posts at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago.

Karen O'Brien-Kop earned her PhD at SOAS (~2014–2018) under Theodore N. Proferes, Ulrich Pagel, and James Mallinson. She was a senior teaching fellow at SOAS (~2018–2020) and a lecturer at the University of Roehampton (~2020–2022).

Karin Meyers is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Jay L. Garfield. From ~2010 to 2017, she was an assistant professor and MA program director at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
Karin Preisendanz is an Indologist and philosopher. She held a post at the University of Hamburg (~1993–1999) and served as professor at the University of Vienna (~1999–2023).

Karl Ammer (1911–1970) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Vienna (~1930–1936). He taught Wolfgang Morgenroth and served as a professor at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1957–1970).
